It evokes the idea of striving for truthfulness in one's actions, intentions, and words. Furthermore, the association with 'sadaqa', the act of giving to charity or providing alms, is an essential component of Islam and a way of purifying one's heart and connecting with God. He described Sedik as a scholar of Hadith and a venerated teacher in Damascus. He was known for his accurate transmission of Hadith and his insightful commentary on them.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hadid mentioned Sedik ibn Al-Harith al-Asadi in his book 'Al-Muhit fi Tawil Asma' al-Rasul', written around 1252 CE.
